newsitem.title: USA: UAL weighs wage hike for salaried workers.
newsitem.headline: UAL weighs wage hike for salaried workers.

text.p: UAL Corp said Friday discussions were under way about a possible wage increase for its 33,000 salaried and non-union employees, following agreements reached with two of its unions.
UAL spokesman Tony Molinaro said management was discussing possible wage hikes for salaried employees. UAL is the parent of United Airlines.

Earlier, UAL reached a tentative agreement with the International Association of Machinists (IAM), calling for wage increases of three percent in 1997 and 1998 and two percent in 1999 and 2000. The IAM represents 24,000 UAL workers.
In late November, it reached a similar wage increase agreement with the Air Line Pilots Association, covering 8,500 United pilots.
Donaldson, Lufkin and Jenrette analyst James Higgins said the wage increase for the machinists was a little higher than he expected.
"I would have liked to see a little less," Higgins added. "It does place some pressure on their (UAL's) costs."

The agreement with the machinists, like the pact with the pilots, was part of a mid-term wage adjustment under UAL's employee stock ownership plan. That wage adjustment was built into UAL's July 1994 employee stock ownership plan (ESOP), when the pilots, machinists and salaried employees swapped wage cuts and work rule changes for a majority stake in the airline.
United's flight attendants are not part of the agreement.
UAL's Molinaro said at the time of the ESOP, pay rates were cut to below industry standards, although employees did receive stock that has appreciated in value.
"This (wage adjustment) is just to make sure the gap doesn't widen further between us and the industry," he said.
UAL shares were down 1-3/4 at 61-1/4 in late afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange, after closing Thursday near its 52-week high.
